question: Foreign share for the 71 non-Q top-500 recipients with no Form 990 ($4.943bn DAF inbound): The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints entities, Campus Crusade for Christ (Cru), Wycliffe Bible Translators, Catholic Relief Services, Salvation Army entities, four Chan Zuckerberg Biohub/Institute LLCs, state universities and hospitals; take foreign programme spending from audited financial statements or annual reports (2023+), else from a parent's Form 990
conclusion_affected: Combined share of DAF money reaching abroad (5.20% measured; non-filer step 6.53% [I])
rationale: These recipients count as zero in the measured figure and at the non-Q average 7.6% in [I]; CRS, Cru, Wycliffe and LDS humanitarian work likely spend far more abroad, the CZ Biohubs far less, so the 7.6% imputation is a guess in both directions

question: Replace the beyond-500 extrapolation with a census or stratified sample: parse Part IX line 3/25 and Schedule F Part I for non-Q recipients ranked 501-2,000 (cut-off $16.16m; Global Fund for Children is 791st) and a random sample of ranks 2,001+
conclusion_affected: Upper end of DAF money abroad (8.41% [I] rests on a 4.30% tail share applied to $42.8bn)
rationale: The last [I-extrap] step adds $1.842bn, more than the measured non-Q total, on the share of just the last 100 parsed ranks; the distribution is concentrated (top 25 = 65.8% of non-Q dollars) so a tail share may be far too high or too low

question: Second-hop look-through for re-granting non-Q recipients (The Clear Fund/GiveWell, ClimateWorks, New Venture Fund, Windward Fund, Hopewell Fund, RF Catalytic Capital, Founders Pledge, Bright Funds Foundation, Gates Philanthropy Partners): read their Schedule I for grants to US Q/friends organisations and apply the receivers' filed foreign shares
conclusion_affected: Whether DAF money through grantmaker intermediaries reaches abroad via US NGOs (counted as domestic in this run)
rationale: Each DAF dollar is counted only at its first recipient's own foreign spending; a fiscal sponsor's or grantmaker's grant to e.g. a US relief NGO is line 1 (domestic) on its return, so money abroad via two US hops is uncounted

question: University foreign campuses through related entities: for Cornell, NYU, Georgetown, Carnegie Mellon, Northwestern, Duke and Johns Hopkins, read Schedule R (related organisations, foreign domicile) and campus financial reports to measure campus spending not in Schedule F Part I; also check unusually large Part I 'Program services' rows (Wesleyan FY2023 $444.0m above total expenses; Caltech Europe $58-98m a year)
conclusion_affected: University foreign share (3.6% for 86 non-Q education recipients, $140.4m abroad)
rationale: Part I is self-labelled; one capped Wesleyan row looks like mislabelled offshore investments, and campuses held in separate legal entities may be missing from Part I

question: DAF sponsors among recipients: for the 42 DAFRC-panel recipients in the non-Q top 500 ($6.460bn inbound; Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors, Global Greengrants, Nature Conservancy, Johns Hopkins) and 11 own-DAF holders (Part IV line 6 Yes), split inbound into DAF-held and spent using Schedule D Part I contributions/grants, then decide whether to add their $187.4m abroad to the headline
conclusion_affected: Headline vs sensitivity (5.20% vs 5.39% with sponsors)
rationale: DAF-to-DAF money that sits in a second DAF before going abroad is excluded from the headline; DAFRC panel and Part IV line 6 tests disagree for re-granting platforms (Bright Funds Foundation answers No), and Chicago Community Foundation (no 990 under its Schedule I EIN) is caught by neither
